20260816-ts-x470d4u-v4-0-cd08e78287ec@si.subject: [PATCH v4 0/2] ARM: dts: aspeed: ASRock Rack X470D4U BMC support

blocks.text:
This series adds support for the BMC of the ASRock Rack X470D4U mainboard,
which uses an ASPEED AST2500.

The mainboard exists in three known flavors, the "normal" X470D4U, the
X470D4U2-2T (with 2x10G RJ45) and the X470D4U2/1N1 (an ODM version with
2x1G RJ45 that is now available in retail). The 1N1 version also has a 64MB
BMC SPI by default, but they are all swappable.

There are two device trees, one that has all the config and uses a 32MB
flash layout, and another one called "data64" (similar to facebook-fuji)
that uses the 64MB flash layout.
Please note that this board has been fully reverse-engineered.

Thanks,
Tan
Signed-off-by: Tan Siewert <tan@siewert.io>

20260816-ts-x470d4u-v4-2-cd08e78287ec@si.subject: [PATCH v4 2/2] ARM: dts: aspeed: add asrock x470d4u bmc

blocks.text:
The ASRock Rack X470D4U X470D4U is a single-socket X470-based microATX
motherboard for Ryzen processors with an AST2500 BMC and either 32MB or
64MB SPI flash.

This mainboard exists in three known "flavors" which only differ in the
used host NIC, the BMC SPI size and some parts that may be un-populated.

To allow the use of the full SPI flash, add two trees, one of which has
the 32M layout with the base config, and a 64M tree that includes the
base tree.
Signed-off-by: Tan Siewert <tan@siewert.io>

20260816111210.2441D1F000E9@smtp.kernel..subject: Re: [PATCH v4 1/2] dt-bindings: arm: aspeed: add ASRock X470D4U BMC

blocks.text:
Thank you for your contribution! Sashiko AI review found 1 potential issue(s) to consider:
- [Low] The invalid compatible string `asrock,x470d4u-data64-bmc` is improperly added to the dt-bindings UAPI.
--

--- Patch [1]: [PATCH v4 1/2] dt-bindings: arm: aspeed: add ASRock X470D4U BMC ---
commit d0559c4cf1eefd31825e79b49e2443b883b69be6
Author: Tan Siewert <tan@siewert.io>
dt-bindings: arm: aspeed: add ASRock X470D4U BMC

This commit documents ASRock's X470D4U BMC board compatibles in the Aspeed
device tree binding schema.

[Severity: Low]
Is this compatible string factually correct for ASRock hardware?

The "-data64" suffix is typically used exclusively by Facebook/Meta hardware
to denote a specific 64MB SPI NOR flash layout in OpenBMC (e.g.,
"facebook,wedge400-data64-bmc").

Could this pollute the stable UAPI/dt-binding schema with a fictitious
device configuration for standard ASRock X470D4U hardware?
Sashiko AI review · https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260816-ts-x470d4u-v4-0-cd08e78287ec@siewert.io?part=1
